Subject: Post-call: Performance/SLO follow-up + proposed SLA language

Thanks for the time today — good conversation. As promised, quick recap of the perf/SLO items we discussed and next steps.

Recap of ask & target metrics (as we understood):
- Latency targets: p95 <= 150ms (time-to-first-token), p99 <= 350ms (completion) for typical text generation workloads (avg request ~256 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained 200 requests/sec (avg seq len 256) with expected burst to 500rps.
- Concurrency: support 50 concurrent streaming sessions without head-of-line impact.
- Streaming: must deliver first token within target and maintain steady token emission rate; client-side buffering acceptable but server should not stall.

Open/clarifying items we flagged:
- How you want latency measured (server ingress vs. end-to-end including client network).
- Acceptable maintenance windows and exclusions for SLA.
- Preferred reporting cadence and remedy structure (credits vs. engineering support).

Attachments: ACME-Redwood-SLA-Draft-v1.pdf (draft language), latency-measurement-diagram.png

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the targets above and call out any workload variants (very long sequences, heavy embedding mix) by EOD Tue.
2) I’ll send a proposed SLA language with definitions for "latency measurement", "exclusions", and "reporting cadence" — please review and suggest edits.
3) If acceptable, we’ll loop in Legal for final redlines and Procurement for T&Cs.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — great summary.

A couple quick clarifications before we review the draft:
1) Measurement: we prefer "edge-to-edge" (from our client SDK send time to client receive first-byte) for product guarantees. Is Redwood able to provide both server-side and client-side metrics? If not, will server-side measurement be acceptable to our SREs?
2) Exclusions: please clarify what you consider "scheduled maintenance" (notice period, max monthly time). Also want to confirm exclusion for customer-caused incidents (e.g., hitting concurrency limits).
3) Remedies: procurement will push for a clearer, formulaic credit table tied to minutes of outage or % of requests over thresholds. Can you propose numbers (and any caps)?

We’ll review the draft SLA once you send it. For context, our target go-live window is early Jan, so we need final terms by mid-December.

Appreciate it —

Alex — thanks, good questions. Attached is a first-pass with explicit definitions; summary below.

Measurement
- Primary measurement point: server-side ingress timestamp (Redwood edge) to first-token and to completion. We can additionally provide client-side telemetry if Acme embeds our SDK — that will be treated as supplemental evidence rather than the contractual measurement.
- Rationale: server-side measurement ensures consistent, auditable measurement across regions and customers. We log per-request telemetry (timestamps, model variant, region) and can provide monthly export.

Exclusions (examples):
- Scheduled maintenance with >=72 hours notice (not to exceed 6 hours/month).
- Force majeure events (e.g., regional cloud outage outside Redwood control).
- Customer-caused issues: malformed requests, extreme burst traffic beyond agreed concurrency/throughput without prior notice, or credentials misconfiguration.

Reporting cadence & notifications
- Monthly SLA report: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, request counts, regional breakdowns.
- Near-real-time dashboard access for SREs + 24-hour incident notification for any SLA-impacting event.

Remedies
- Uptime-style credits: for any full-hour window where availability drops below agreed threshold, 5% credit of monthly invoice per hour, up to 50% cap.
- Performance breaches (latency targets): graduated credits based on percentage of requests breaching p95 target across the month — e.g., 5% credit for 1-5% breach, 10% for 5-10%, etc. (see attached table in draft).
- Credits applied to next billing cycle; no cash payouts. We’re open to negotiating caps for enterprise deals.

I’ve attached ACME-Redwood-SLA-Draft-v1.pdf with the exact contract language and a simple diagram for measurement points. Please review and flag any redlines; Rishi/Vivek — if you have suggestions on the remedy caps or alternative formulas, pls share.

Next steps: if Acme is broadly aligned, I can set up a 30-min legal sync next week to run through contract language.

Thanks,
Marissa
